items.actClause: AN ACT to authorize the commissioner of general services to transfer and convey certain unappropriated state land to the Cedarmore Corporation for community programs ;.us on;
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6318

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to authorize the commissioner of general
services to transfer and convey certain unappropriated state land to
the Cedarmore Corporation for community programs

 PURPOSE :

To allow the transfer of the Freeport Armory to the Cedarmore
Corporation, for its development as a center to house non-profit
corporations and various community programs.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 authorizes the Commissioner of General Services to transfer
the Freeport Armory to the Cedermore Corporation in consideration of
one-dollar.

Section 2 contains the deed description of the Freeport Armory.

Section 3 explains that section 2 is not intended to be a legal
description of the property, but is provided only to identify said
property.

Section 4 provides a one-year window in which Cedarmore Corporation
may apply to OGS for purchase of the Armory.

Sections 5 and 6 detail how the structure may be used by Cedarmore
Corporation. Section 7 provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The Freeport Armory was home to a National Guard unit, but has been
without a permanent tenant since 2011. The property has suffered
damage as a result of numerous natural disasters, and has most
recently been leased as storage space of heavy equipment. This bill
would allow for the property to be conveyed to Cedarmore Corporation.
As a condition of the conveyance, Cedarmore Corporation is required to
provide office space free-of-charge to the Delta Sigma Theta Sorority,
Inc., and the Nassau County American Legion. The bill limits the use
of the building to not-for-profit family and youth service
organizations and/or recreational programs and for public safety.

This legislation provides a mechanism for the Freeport Armory to be
transferred to Cedarmore Corporation and used for various community
programs. Should Cedarmore cease to use the property for its intended
purposes, title shall revert back to the State.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the State

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.
